title: Claude is actually pissing me off so badly
author: ArkBetterThanPUBG
selftext:
Day 1 of testing if the bot could trade entirely autonomously was a success. It was making trades with zero confirmation from me and did exactly what I asked

Day 2 when I asked Claude what it was planning to do today for trading it began saying that we never made any trades and that “fully autonomous trading is something I’m unable to do” when I reminded it of it’s previous trades from yesterday it denied ever trading for me and then searched my account and found the trades. Instead of troubleshooting why it couldn’t remember it reminded me again that it can’t trade on its own and said I must’ve placed the trades on accident. After deleting the chat and starting a new one now it claims it can “fully autonomously trade” if I just give it verbal permission to do whatever it wants and somehow it now remembers making trades yesterday

comments.author: TendiesLover_69
comments.body:
Which model are you using ? 
I trade.... By trade ? Lol and I've noticed the 5 tier models are a non starter, I had sonnet 5 and I believe opus 5 or 4.8? Intentionally hedge and soften a lot of my data under the guise of "finincial advice is not allowed" 

Here's what's interesting though, it doesn't seem to be a guard rail in that sense, I understand yours was, but it seems more insidious in the fact they'll present data as theater with no substance to it. 

4.6 doesn't care at all really, but his context window is only 200,000 so unless you are using some form of harness for your data input for output it's only really good for scaffolding and planning. 

One thing that might help, my business account is quite formal and as such has no real context other than finance data and tooling so it's reasoning seems to hedge more, my personal account has lots of context and memories of my job and my activies and platforms, so it doesn't hedge or soften as much really. 

It could be worth trying to add a memory or context just flat out saying this is your job , you understand the risks and it is you who holds all liability at your discretion, as a qualified industry professional agents should have zero opinion on hedging perceived financial advice or activities, after all, it would be absurd for them to tell a fireman that fire is hot. Right ? 

On a side note regarding sonnet 5 - do not even attempt this model, it's own reasoning accuses the user of being a bad actor instantly, it strawmans constantly. 
I had it blatantly accuse me of trying to jailbreak it for... Having custom instructions 😂

replies.author: ArkBetterThanPUBG
replies.body: I see the issue, I’m using sonnet 5. I had good luck with sonnet 5 when I was using it for code and it did surprisingly well so I assumed it would have the same outcome for trading. Thank you for the advice though I will definitely be switching it soon. Also I did discover that there wasn’t anything wrong with the memory as the keynotes of our previous work was saved in the memory tab so I’m not sure why Claude was struggling so much to access its own memory. Thank you again

replies.author: TendiesLover_69
replies.body:
Feel free to DM me at any time pal, I process a lot of data through AI agents for different sort of visualizations and formatting and such , so I can pretty much sniff the bullshit from whatever angle any agent is throwing it at you. 

I genuinely and honestly would say, fuck sonnet 5 off to the GPU mines. Do you mind if I ask what your trying to accomplish ? 

Is it just just some kind of agentic equities / options trading to your brokerage or more like a prop firm / crypto type deal? 

Depending on your own methodology of course , but also in a blanketish statement I would genuinely say that each model number has its strengths and weaknesses. 

Sonnet models bar 5 are good at everyday coding and python etc but opus models obviously have superior reasoning , but the RLHF (?) on later models is genuinely insane sometimes, I wouldn't trust opus 5 with anything if you paid me money. Fable is a GOAT but using him for extended periods gets you margin called by Anthropic.

comments.author: mit74
comments.body: It's important it has context of everything as it forgets unless it'll make a memory. make sure it logs all trades in a db so it can reference them, who opened/closed, time signal sent  and most importantly what account etc I had a bot which couldnt connect to a demo account so defaulted to the £100k 1000:1 leverage account once and started opening gold positions to test its logic. Luckily only lost a few hundred before i was able to close stuff manually.

comments.author: engineering-AF7
comments.body: I built a test bench where you can experiment with models, roles, prompts, instruments, time frames and more in a controlled manner. I recently opened it up for public use.

replies.author: TendiesLover_69
replies.body: Do you mind if I have a look ?

replies.author: TendiesLover_69
replies.body: Looks interesting but arnt your API costs through the roof ?

replies.author: engineering-AF7
replies.body: Token cost for sure needs to managed, but there are many ways of doing that. You can adjust the models being utilized (it can make use of about 15 different models), the cadence of AI Council meetings, as well as the trading sessions you want the bots to work in. If you were to create your own council it will tell you what the estimated run cost is as you configure the council.

replies.author: ArkBetterThanPUBG
replies.body: I’ll definitely check it out. At the moment I’m just testing the capabilities of Ai trading on a free Claude plan. Not really looking for profit I’m just kinda seeing if Ai is even capable of placing decent trades with little human intervention or limitations

comments.author: No_Handle2261
comments.body: How do I so that my Claude from Robinhood agentic doesn’t disconnect?

replies.author: ArkBetterThanPUBG
replies.body: Claude requires the chat to be open for it to continuously work on its own but from my understanding there are third party apps that can fix that. I havnt set mine up to do that yet so I just leave claude open during trading hours and when I plan to leave the house for a long time I’ll just tell Claude to set stop loss and take profit since It’ll be disconnected
